newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Australian bonds continue downside probes.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Australian bonds continue downside probes.

text.p: *Australian bond futures ended SYCOM with modest gains, but the rise was seen as insufficient to suggest that this week's downside tests were over.
*The 10-year bond contract again survived probes to the 93.470 to 93.450 support area.
Australian bond futures ended SYCOM with modest gains, but the rise was seen as insufficient to suggest that this week's downside tests were over.
The September 10-year bond futures contract ended after-hours trade at 93.500, and up from Tuesday's 93.485 pit close, and again survived probes to the 93.470 to 93.450 support area.

The contract needs to crack immediate resistance at 93.510 to put the market on a firmer footing and breakout from a mini-downward sloping channel that has been created since last week's record peak of 93.640, analysts said.
The 10-year bond briefly dropped to 93.440, which coincided with a sell-off in U.S. Treasuries after the second quarter U.S. employment costs index rose 0.8 percent.
While this was in line with economists' expectations the market had been hoping for a weaker outcome, as had been the case in the previous quarter when costs rose just 0.6 percent.
However, the U.S. market later recovered, taking local bonds with it, as the July consumer confidence index fell, and were helped on by flows from the mortgage backed securities market.
Meanwhile, local June building approvals data are due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Expectations centre on a 1.5 percent fall after the 2.2 percent rise in May, according to a Reuters survey of economists.

However, more importance is being put on Thursday's June and quarterly trade reports, which are expected to enforce expectations of a 1/2 point rate cut after next week's RBA board meeting, and may even raise thoughts of another easing down the track if they prove exceptionally weak, analysts added.
